A field guide to an inhabited world · volume XV · the reptile family

Lizardfolk

Five scaly monster girls with lizard tails: the salamander of the lava, the vanishing chameleon, the fast iguana, the deadly crocodile and the turtle who hides in her shell. Cold-blooded, sun-loving and much tougher than they look.

Favourite food: Eggs (any egg) and fish

The central similarity

Warm up first.

Lizardfolk are cold-blooded: sunlight and heat make them quick, cold makes them sluggish. Every one of them basks.

  • BaskingIn sunlight or near fire they bask and heal; in cold biomes they are slower.
  • TailsA heavy tail for balance and swimming; the salamander's burns.
  • EggsThe family food: any egg (a turtle prefers seagrass).
  • ScalesNatural armour: every lizardfolk has some armour points.

Relationships (shared by every family)

The same relationship core runs through all MonsterGirls families, from the harpies on. This volume only changes how a lizardfolk builds trust, what she gives back, and how she bears young.

AffectionEach monster girl remembers every player separately. Feeding, petting and her family's own bond action raise it; hurting her lowers it. /monstergirls bonds lists everyone nearby.
SitRight-click any monster girl with a plain stick to make her sit; again to let her get up.
Sharing a bedAt high friendship (25) she may join you in bed: once a night she decides, one in three at 25, certain at 100. Sleep through the night and she is expecting.
ExpectingA pregnancy lasts one in-game day. Her belly rounds out as it goes on (the model shows it).
Born devotedHer young are born devoted to the player who fathered them (full affection) and never share that player's bed.
PresentsAt high friendship every family brings presents of its own kind.
BondAffectionWhat it means
Wild0Keeps her distance; her species' instincts decide everything.
Curious3+Lets you come close and watches what you do.
Fond10+Follows you a little way, accepts petting, stops fleeing.
High friendship25+May join you in bed at night (one night in three, more the fonder she is) and brings presents.
Devoted60+The family's devoted perk unlocks (see each guide).
Full devotion100The most there is. Every daughter feels this for the player who fathered her.

Friendship

What builds trust

  • Eggs (+1), turtle eggs and laid harpy eggs (+2), fish (+1)
  • A warm spot (a campfire) she can bask by

What costs trust

  • Hitting her
  • Splashing her in cold water

Devoted (60+)

She shares her toughness: Resistance I while she is near you in a fight, and she brings shed scales (scutes).

Mating & young

FormA leathery clutch. Young2-4 hatchlings, grown in 5 days. WhereWarm sand or dirt (the salamander: netherrack). Hatchlings use the adult model at 45%.

1. CourtshipAt high friendship she may share your bed (warmth is the best gift).
2. EggsShe lays a leathery clutch of two to four eggs in warm sand or dirt (the salamander in the Nether).
3. HatchingAfter a day the hatchlings break out, each a random colour of her species.
4. GrownGrown in five days.

Behaviour & gameplay (shared by the family)

Cold-bloodedFaster and regenerating in sunlight or within four blocks of fire or lava; Slowness in cold biomes.
StealthThe chameleon turns invisible while standing still.
Death rollIn water, the crocodile grabs her prey and rolls: it is held in place and takes heavy damage.
ShellThe turtle pulls into her shell when hurt (80% less damage, no movement) and lays her eggs on beaches.
Fire tailThe salamander's tail is a flame: fireproof, she lights what she hits and gives off light.

Salamander (about 1.7 blocks)

TemperamentHot-headed, bold, warm

Ecology & behaviourThe fire salamander of legend, whose tail is a living flame. She bathes in lava.

Signature: Fire tailFireproof, swims in lava, glows. Her hits set things alight.

Player interactionMeet her near lava; bring eggs.

Chameleon (about 1.6 blocks)

TemperamentShy, watchful, dry humour

Crocodile (about 2.2 blocks)

TemperamentPatient, aggressive, toothy grin

Ecology & behaviourThe apex predator of the riverbanks. She waits half-submerged and strikes.

Signature: Death rollHostile at first. In water she grabs prey and rolls: held fast and badly hurt. Fed meat, she calms; fed more, she is fiercely loyal.

Player interactionFeed her fish from the bank. Never swim near a wild one.

Swamps & mangrovesPatient · ancient

Alligator Snapping Turtle (about 1.8 blocks)

TemperamentPatient, grumpy, very old

Ecology & behaviourMacrochelys temminckii (Testudines: Chelydridae), the largest freshwater turtle in North America. She lies still on the riverbed with her mouth open and wiggles a pink, worm-like lure on her tongue until a fish swims in.

Signature: Tongue lureWhile she sits still in water she catches a fish now and then and drops it at her feet (cod or salmon, at most three lying around at a time). Hit her and she hides in her shell. Her bite is the hardest in the family after the crocodile's.

Player interactionLeave her be in the water and she will feed you. Bring her fish.

Colour variants

Common (default) · Dark brown shell, olive skinMossy · Algae on her shell and hairDark · Almost blackSuwannee · The Suwannee River species, paler and greyerLeucistic · Pale cream, very rare

Spawns inswamp, mangrove_swamp

DangerModerate if provoked (a hard bite).

Rivers & swampsPolite · mischievous

Kappa (about 1.5 blocks)

TemperamentMischievous, proud, very polite

Ecology & behaviourA river yokai of Japan: a turtle's shell on her back and a dish of water (the sara) on her head. Folklore says it comes from the softshell turtle (Pelodiscus sinensis, Testudines: Trionychidae) and the Japanese giant salamander.

Signature: Her dishWet (water, rain) she is strong. Two minutes dry and her dish has run empty: she is weak and slow. Bow to her and she bows back, spilling it: a kappa who was after you stops at once.

Player interactionBow to her (crouch while facing her): she bows back. Melon slices stand in for her beloved cucumbers.

Colour variants

River (default) · Green shell and hairPond · TealRed · A red kappaMountain · BrownWhite · Rare and pale

Spawns inriver, swamp

DangerModerate in the water, low out of it.

Red-Eared Slider (about 1.4 blocks)

TemperamentSociable, easily startled

Ecology & behaviourTrachemys scripta elegans (Testudines: Emydidae), the pond turtle with the red streak behind each eye, named for sliding off her log into the water at the first sign of trouble.

Signature: Sliding offSliders bask together by the water. When a stranger comes within 6 blocks, every slider nearby slides into the nearest water at once. Every food is worth double to her.

Player interactionFish and kelp. Walk up slowly.

Galapagos Tortoise (about 1.95 blocks)

TemperamentAncient, patient, unhurried

Ecology & behaviourChelonoidis niger (Testudines: Testudinidae), the giant tortoise of the Galapagos, who lives well over a century.

Signature: A ride on her shellThe slowest girl there is, and the toughest. A friend can sit on her shell: she keeps going where she was going. Cactus does not prick her.

In the game

Built (2026-10-19)

  • Cold-blooded: faster and healing in sun or near fire, slow in the cold; basking
  • Scales are armour
  • Eggs (any, the harpies' too) and fish
  • Salamander: fireproof, glows, burns what she hits
  • Chameleon: invisible while still, tongue pulls dropped items over
  • Iguana: the fastest
  • Crocodile: hostile until fed, death roll in water
  • Turtle: shell retreat
  • Leathery clutches in sand or dirt
  • Devoted: Resistance in a fight
  • Anvil tortoise: mends a damaged tool or armour piece by a quarter for one of its repair materials from your inventory, no experience needed; too heavy to push
  • Gecko: fast, climbs walls, curious (trails you and inspects what you drop), sheds her tail when hit
  • Chupacabra: hunts only wild goats, fades from sight when looked at, takes no orders, leaves half stacks of mutton
  • Red-eared slider: a stranger within 6 blocks sends every slider nearby sliding into the water; food is worth double
  • Galapagos tortoise: the slowest and toughest; a friend rides on her shell (empty hand; crouch to pat); cactus does not prick her
  • Box turtle: shut in her shell she takes no damage; a sprinting stranger makes her shut; she stays within 16 blocks of home
  • Softshell: buried out of sight on a sandy riverbed, bites strangers who come close; no armour, quick
  • Matamata: invisible while still in water, gulps fish within 4 blocks (her friend gets them)

Not yet

  • Chameleon colours by biome

Design decisions log

Decided (2026-10-19)

  • Lizardfolk eat eggs, so the harpies' laid eggs are a treat for them.

Open questions

  • Should the chameleon's colours change with the biome?
